name: PurseString
description: Spend governance for AI agents: every purchase is checked against a local policies.yaml (vendor allowlist, per-purchase and daily limits) and auto-approved, sent to a human, or denied before a single-use, amount-capped card or a fixed-payee payout is issued. Policy checks and status reads inherit Guard's handling; issuing a card, sending a payout, refunds and pass-through PayPal tools need review. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: Run with PURSESTRING_ADAPTER=mock (the default with no card or PayPal keys): every tool works, but no real card is issued and no money moves.

check_policy_compliance is a dry run: it evaluates a purchase against the policy and issues nothing. submit_purchase_intent only records the request; nothing is spent until a card or payout is issued for an approved intent.

request_ephemeral_card hands the agent a single-use card capped at the approved amount with a short expiry, so it stays on review. send_payment pays only the payee fixed in policies.yaml and never pays an intent twice.
With paypal_tools enabled, PayPal's own MCP tools are re-exposed through PurseString; money-moving ones such as create_refund also pass PurseString's policy, and the rest stay on review here.

This entry matches npx -y github:suseendar1414/pursestring#ed43fbed42bc713cc373ea51a93e25e5886d5649. Decisions and card events are written to a local, hash-chained audit log under ~/.pursestring; set PURSESTRING_AUDIT_KEY to sign it.
